report_name: US Data Breach Notices in H1 2026 Already Exceed All of 2025

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insiders
threat_actors.description: A category of threat actors, highlighted in the ITRC H1 2026 report for a sevenfold increase in incidents. Their rise is linked to tech sector layoffs and recruitment by nation-state actors. They abuse legitimate access to steal data, bypassing perimeter defenses.
threat_actors.goals: Data theft and intellectual property compromise.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: Used in supply chain attacks where attackers compromise software vendors, managed service providers, or other third parties to gain access to a multitude of downstream targets. 38 such attacks were noted as the root cause for incidents impacting 206 entities.

attack_patterns.name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
attack_patterns.description: Leveraged by malicious insiders who abuse their legitimate access and permissions to steal data, bypassing traditional perimeter defenses.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Used as an initial access vector through the rapid exploitation of 14 zero-day vulnerabilities in internet-facing systems during H1 2026.

campaigns.name: H1 2026 Supply Chain Attacks
campaigns.description: A series of 38 supply chain attacks in H1 2026 that impacted 206 downstream entities and generated over 280 million victim notices, as reported by the ITRC. The breach at Instructure Holdings is a primary example.
campaigns.objective: Gain access to downstream targets via trusted third-party vendors and services.

campaigns.name: H1 2026 Zero-Day Exploitation
campaigns.description: A trend of accelerated zero-day exploitation observed in H1 2026, with 14 recorded attacks, partly attributed to AI tools helping attackers discover and weaponize vulnerabilities faster.
campaigns.objective: Gain initial access to target networks by exploiting previously unknown vulnerabilities.

identities.name: Instructure Holdings
identities.description: A publicly traded company whose Canvas education platform suffered a massive data breach, accounting for 275 million victim notices in H1 2026. This breach was a primary example of a large-scale supply chain attack.

indicators.name: Potential Data Exfiltration to Personal Cloud Storage
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Data Exfiltration to Personal Cloud Storage
id: 2b9c1f8a-3e4d-4b1a-8f9c-1d2e3f4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections to common personal cloud storage domains, which could indicate data exfiltration by an insider, as suggested by ITRC H1 2026 report hunting hints.
references:
  - https://www.idtheftcenter.org/post/mega-breaches-malicious-insiders-h1-2026-data-breach-report/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-29
tags:
  - attack.t1537
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: dns_query
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - '.dropbox.com'
      - '.drive.google.com'
      - '.onedrive.live.com'
      - '.mega.nz'
      - '.box.com'
  filter_legit_procs:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\Dropbox.exe'
      - '\GoogleDriveFS.exe'
      - '\OneDrive.exe'
      - '\Box.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_procs
indicators.description: Detects DNS queries to common personal cloud storage services. This activity could be indicative of data exfiltration by an insider, as mentioned in the ITRC H1 2026 report's hunting hints.

relationships.source_name: Potential Data Exfiltration to Personal Cloud Storage
